content: Clarithromycin should be used with caution in patients who are concurrently treated with drugs that prolong the QT interval and have known arrhythmogenic properties. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of paclitaxel by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitoring is recommended. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of protein-bound paclitaxel through similar mechanisms involving CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein. Caution and monitoring are advised. Vonoprazan increases the levels or effects of pacritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. It is a weak CYP3A inhibitor, so caution is necessary when co-administering with sensitive CYP3A substrates. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of paliperidone by affecting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Both clarithromycin and paliperidone prolong the QTc interval, necessitating therapy modification and close monitoring. Clarithromycin increases panobinostat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The starting dose of panobinostat should be reduced to 10 mg when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Therapy should be modified and closely monitored. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of pantothenic acid by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of parecoxib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of paricalcitol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of paromomycin by affecting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is recommended. Clarithromycin and paroxetine both prolong the QTc interval, requiring therapy modification and close monitoring. Clarithromycin and pasireotide both prolong the QTc interval, necessitating therapy modification and close monitoring. Clarithromycin and pazopanib both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of perampanel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. Vonoprazan increases the levels or effects of pimozide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. It is a weak CYP3A inhibitor, so caution is necessary when co-administering with sensitive CYP3A substrates. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of pimozide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of pioglitazone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. Vonoprazan decreases the levels or effects of polysaccharide iron by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Monitoring is advised. Clarithromycin decreases the effects of piperacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. Monitoring is recommended. Clarithromycin increases the toxicity of pitavastatin through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition, which may increase the risk of myopathy. Monitoring is advised. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of polatuzumab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to small peptides, amino acids, monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), and unconjugated MMAE-related catabolites. MMAE is a CYP3A4 substrate, and co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase unconjugated MMAE AUC, potentially increasing polatuzumab vedotin toxicities. Monitoring is recommended. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of posaconazole by affecting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Both clarithromycin and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval, necessitating therapy modification and close monitoring. Clarithromycin increases pravastatin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for myopathy, and do not exceed a pravastatin dose of 40 mg/day when co-administered with clarithromycin. OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase the risk of myopathy. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of praziquantel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of prednisolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and affecting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Risk of toxic steroid concentrations and altered mental status necessitates caution and monitoring. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of prednisone by affecting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter and decreasing metabolism. Monitoring is advised. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of propafenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Monitoring is advised. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of quazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. Clarithromycin and quetiapine both increase the QTc interval. Avoid use with drugs that prolong QT and in patients with risk factors for prolonged QT interval. Postmarketing cases show QT prolongation with overdose in patients with concomitant illness or with drugs known to cause electrolyte imbalance or prolong QT. Vonoprazan increases the levels or effects of quinidine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. It is a weak CYP3A inhibitor, so caution is necessary when co-administering with sensitive CYP3A substrates. Clarithromycin and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Monitoring is recommended. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of quizartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Monitor patients more frequently with ECG if co-administered with QT-prolonging drugs. Vonoprazan increases the levels or effects of repaglinide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. It is a weak CYP3A inhibitor, so caution is necessary when co-administering with sensitive CYP3A substrates. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of rabeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. Clarithromycin and ranolazine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. Clarithromycin increases rifaximin levels by affecting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is recommended. Clarithromycin increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of clarithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution is advised when rilpivirine is co-administered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of riociguat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ripretinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with a strong CYP3A inhibitor increases systemic exposure to ripretinib and its active metabolite (DP-5439), which may increase the risk of adverse reactions. Monitoring is advised. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of risperidone by affecting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Both clarithromycin and risperidone prolong the QTc interval, necessitating therapy modification and close monitoring. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by affecting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is recommended. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of roflumilast by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of romidepsin by affecting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Both clarithromycin and romidepsin prolong the QTc interval, requiring therapy modification and close monitoring. Clarithromycin increases rosiglitazone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This may result in hypoglycemia; glucose levels should be closely monitored. Rucaparib increases clarithromycin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of sacubitril/valsartan through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition. Co-administration with OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase valsartan systemic exposure. Monitoring is recommended. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of salmeterol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both clarithromycin and salmeterol prolong the QTc interval, necessitating caution and monitoring. Clarithromycin increases saxagliptin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Clarithromycin increases seladelpar levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised in patients who are poor CYP2C9 metabolizers and are co-administered a moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Selpercatinib increases clarithromycin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Monitoring is recommended. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of silodosin by affecting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is advised. Vonoprazan increases the levels or effects of sirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. It is a weak CYP3A inhibitor, so caution is necessary when co-administering with sensitive CYP3A substrates. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of sirolimus by affecting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is recommended. Clarithromycin decreases the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering metabolism. Co-administration with antibiotics decreases efficacy by altering colonic bacterial flora needed to convert sodium picosulfate to its active form. Monitoring is advised. Vonoprazan increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. It is a weak CYP3A inhibitor, so caution is necessary when co-administering with sensitive CYP3A substrates. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by affecting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is recommended. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus ointment by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of tamoxifen by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, which decreases the metabolism of tamoxifen to N-desmethyl tamoxifen (an active metabolite with similar biological activity). Monitoring is recommended. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of tasimelteon by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. Tazemetostat decreases clarithromycin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. Tecovirimat decreases clarithromycin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be monitored for effectiveness if co-administered. Clarithromycin and telavancin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of teniposide by affecting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitoring is recommended. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of terbinafine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of tezacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary.
